reasons: A correctly states that a pg_hba.conf rejection produces a different FATAL error. B wrongly lists pg_hba.conf as a cause of the same refused-connection error. B also uses English section headings and paraphrases the error in English, though it better explains why the error means a reject rather than a drop (RST vs timeout).

A: Suggests a Homebrew/source config path ~/Postgres/*/postgresql.conf, which is not a standard location
B: Claims a missing pg_hba.conf rule gives the same 'connection refused' error; it actually yields 'FATAL: pg_hba.conf rejects connection' / 'no pg_hba.conf entry'
Says scram-sha-256 became the default in PostgreSQL 16+; it became the default password_encryption in PostgreSQL 14
Labels 'systemctl restart postgresql-16' as the Debian command; Debian uses postgresql or postgresql@16-main
